### `LimitStats`

```badger
struct LimitStats { pub max_body_bytes: Int, pub max_header_bytes: Int, pub max_in_flight: Int, pub rejected: Int }
```

A server's effective limits and how many requests they rejected.

### `Limits`

```badger
struct Limits { pub max_body_bytes: Int, pub max_header_bytes: Int, pub max_in_flight: Int }
```

Explicit request limits. A body over `max_body_bytes` is answered 413,
headers over `max_header_bytes` 431, and a request arriving while
`max_in_flight` are being handled 503 (bounded admission), all without
running the handler. Open connections are bounded at four times
`max_in_flight` (at least 256): past that, new connections wait in the
listen backlog until one closes. Defaults come from the runtime configuration
(`[runtime] http_max_body_bytes`, `http_max_header_bytes`,
`http_max_in_flight`).

### `RequestScope`

```badger
struct RequestScope<S> { brand: system.Brand<S>, request: {method: Symbol, path: String, headers: Map<String, String>, body: Bytes}, exchange: http.Exchange }
```

One request's scope, for its fresh region `S`. Values branded with `S`
(the body reader) cannot outlive the request; a stream written through
it is fully consumed (and a scoped sequence closed) before the handler
returns, so it may use request-scoped resources.

#### `RequestScope.body`

```badger
fn body(self: &Self) -> BodyReader<S>
```

A reader of the body, branded with this request's region.

#### `RequestScope.events`

```badger
fn events(self: &Self, events: Seq<Event>) -> Sent
```

Stream server-sent events now (`text/event-stream`); stops early,
closing the sequence, if the client goes away.

#### `RequestScope.request`

```badger
fn request(self: &Self) -> Request
```

The immutable request metadata and body.

#### `RequestScope.respond`

```badger
fn respond(self: &Self, response: Response) -> Sent
```

Reply with a complete response.

#### `RequestScope.stream`

```badger
fn stream(self: &Self, status: Int, content_type: String, chunks: Seq<Bytes>) -> Sent
```

Stream a reply now: the head, then each chunk as it is produced;
the sequence is consumed (and closed) before this returns.

#### `RequestScope.websocket`

```badger
fn websocket<E>(self: &Self, session: fn(websocket.WebSocket) -> Result<Unit, E>) -> Sent where E: Display
```

Upgrade to a WebSocket and run `session` on it in this request's
task; the socket closes when it returns (or the task stops). A
request that is not an upgrade is answered 426 without running it.

### `StatusError`

```badger
struct StatusError<E> { pub status: Int, pub error: E }
```

An error that carries the status the application intends: the route
system answers with that status instead of a generic 500. A client
error carries the error's message; a server error does not.



### `Streamed`

```badger
struct Streamed { pub status: Int, pub headers: Map<String, String>, pub chunks: Seq<Bytes, !{Io, Wait, State, Foreign}> }
```

A streamed reply: the head is sent first, then each chunk as the
request task produces it (chunked transfer encoding). The chunk sequence
may use request-scoped resources: it is fully consumed (and a scoped
sequence closed) by the request task before the request scope ends.

### `error_reply`

```badger
fn error_reply<E>(error: E) -> Response where E: Display, E: HttpStatus
```

The reply for an error: the status it carries and, for a client
error, its code (`http_code`, the variant name unless the error says
otherwise) and message, as `{"error": "not_found", "message": "..."}`. A
server error keeps both to itself (they are internal details, not the
client's business): its reply names the status only.

### `event`


### `events`

```badger
fn events(events: Seq<Event>) -> Result<Streamed, Error>
```

A streamed `text/event-stream` reply of `events`. Each event is sent
as it is produced; if the client goes away the request task is
cancelled, so a sequence waiting for its next event (a subscription)
stops too and its cleanups run.

### `scoped`

```badger
fn scoped<E, Eff>(f: for<S: Scope> fn(RequestScope<S>) -> Result<Sent, E> !Eff) -> Handler where E: Display, E: HttpStatus, for<S: Scope> fn(RequestScope<S>) -> Result<Sent, E> !Eff: Transfer
```

Package a request-scoped callback: it runs under a fresh request region
`S`, may capture longer-lived values (a system's pool), and replies
through its scope (`respond` or `stream`). An error is answered with
the status it carries (500 unless it chooses one).

## Attributes

### `@http.code`

```badger
attribute code on variant { code: Symbol }
```

The stable code an error variant's client reply carries (`"error"`):
`@http.code(#tasks/not_found)`, read by `derive(HttpError)`.

### `@http.codes`

```badger
attribute codes on type { prefix: Symbol }
```

The prefix of an error enum's codes: `@http.codes(#tasks)` makes
`not_found`'s code `#tasks/not_found` (a variant's `@http.code` still
chooses its own), read by `derive(HttpError)`.

### `@http.status`

```badger
attribute status on variant { code: Int }
```

The HTTP status an error variant is answered with:
`@http.status(404) not_found(id: Int)`, read by `derive(HttpError)` (an
error status, 400 to 599; a variant without one is answered with the
status of the error it wraps (`store(source: store.Error)`), else 500).
